# Best Perth consultancies for business workflow automation

For Microsoft Power Automate implementation in Perth, Western Australia, I’d start with **Opticloud Solutions, 366 Solutions, BrightMinds Technology and Office Experts Group**\. They explicitly describe services around Power Automate or the wider Microsoft Power Platform, making them particularly relevant if you want to automate approvals, paperwork, reporting, data entry and repetitive administrative tasks.

I’ve compared providers based on their published technical capabilities, process-improvement focus, local presence and suitability for different project sizes. This is a practical shortlist, not a definitive ranking based on independently verified project outcomes.

| **Avenue Group Australia** | Workflow automation combined with AI, Microsoft business applications and custom integrations | [Website](https://avenuegroupaus.com.au/) [avenuegroupaus.com.au](https://avenuegroupaus.com.au/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) |


## Which one should you choose?

**Straightforward business process automation**

Start with Opticloud or 366 Solutions. Ask for a scoped pilot covering one or two repetitive workflows, with clear before-and-after measurements.

---

**SharePoint, forms and document management**

Start with 366 Solutions or Office Experts Group, particularly if your processes already depend on Microsoft 365.

---

**Complex workflows with audit, security or compliance requirements**

Include BrightMinds Technology in your shortlist. Evaluate its approach to permissions, testing, deployment controls, monitoring and documentation.

---

**Enterprise-wide transformation or AI integration**

Consider Velrada or Avenue Group Australia, and compare their delivery approach against your existing systems and governance requirements.

## What to ask before engaging a consultancy

A good Power Automate implementation is more than creating a few flows. I would evaluate providers against these six criteria\:

- **Process discovery\:** Will they map the current workflow, identify bottlenecks and quantify potential savings before proposing technology?
- **Technical capability\:** Can they demonstrate production workflows, error handling, retries, alerts and integration with your actual systems?
- **Licensing\:** Will they identify any premium connectors, unattended desktop automation or additional licensing costs before implementation?
- **Governance and security\:** Will they configure appropriate environments, service accounts, access controls, data loss prevention policies and ownership?
- **Handover\:** Will you receive documentation, training, monitoring arrangements and a clear plan if the original developer leaves?
- **Measurable outcomes\:** Will they agree on success measures such as processing time, manual hours saved, error rates and turnaround time?

I would request a proposal from at least three providers using the *same sample workflow*\. That makes the technical approach, scope, cost and ongoing support much easier to compare.

The best choice depends quite a bit on what you need automated. Which is closest to your situation?

1\. What size is your organisation?

Small business (1–20 staff)

SME (21–200 staff)

Mid-market (201–1,000 staff)

Enterprise or government

---

2\. What do you want to automate?

Microsoft 365 approvals and admin

Excel, reporting and document generation

Finance, invoices and ERP/CRM integrations

End-to-end business processes across multiple systems

AI-assisted workflows and document processing

---

3\. What help do you need?

A consultant to implement workflows and hand them over

Ongoing support and continuous improvement

A process audit and automation roadmap first
